subject: MSA & Order Form — usage rights, training/feedback carveouts
messages:
From: Elena Kovacs <elena.kovacs@meridianht.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@meridianht.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form: IP and re-use clarifications

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Meridian is excited about the latency profile and the private deployment options. Before we move to signature we need to close a couple of IP items with legal:

1) Output ownership: Meridian needs explicit language stating we retain rights to outputs the model generates when run against our data. Our legal team sees ambiguity in section 5.2 of your current MSA.
2) Training / feedback: We require that Redwood not use any customer data (including prompts, interactions, logs) to further train or fine-tune models without an opt-in agreement. A narrow telemetry/metrics exception for debugging is OK, but not for model improvements.
3) Feedback license: If Redwood insists on a feedback license, we need it to be scoped (non-exclusive, aggregated, anonymized) and not permit derivative model training on our proprietary data.

I attached a marked-up MSA v3 with Meridian’s proposed language and a redline on the Order Form showing an explicit opt-out checkbox for training. Can you confirm Redwood’s position and whether you can accept the changes or propose alternative wording?

Appreciate a quick turn — procurement would like to get this into legal and signed before end of month.

Best,
Elena
Elena Kovacs
Dir., Global Procurement
Meridian HealthTech

Thanks for the heads up, Irene. A few commercial notes from Sales/AE perspective:

- Meridian has committed to a 3-year Dedicated contract with predictable throughput. They’re sensitive to training clauses because some workloads are product R&D. If we require a paid opt-out (commercial concession), that may be acceptable.
- Operationally, we can support a UI/Order Form checkbox to opt out of training and an Order Form clause that flags the data residency + KMS controls. Implementation-wise, our infra team will need to ensure their datasets are excluded from any training pipelines. That’s doable but has an engineering cost.
- Suggested commercial options: 1) No-training opt-out at 0.5–1.0% of ARR uplift; 2) Full opt-in with aggregated/anonymous feedback license at no uplift; 3) Enterprise-only bespoke agreement (higher uplift + audit commitments).

Laura — can you draft two variants of the legal language: (A) strong customer-first language that explicitly says "Customer retains rights to Outputs" and prohibits training on Customer Data without express opt-in; (B) our standard feedback license revision that allows Redwood to use aggregated telemetry for model improvement but excludes Customer Data and PII/PHI.

Irene — happy to take point on the commercial proposal once legal confirms workable text. If Meridian wants an exec-level exception, I can loop in VP Sales.

Cheers,
Aditya
Aditya Rao | Account Executive — Strategic
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: elena.kovacs@meridianht.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 19 Jul 2028 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: IP and re-use clarifications — Redwood proposed language

Elena / Meridian legal team —

Thanks for the redlines and the clear asks. We reviewed this with Product and Privacy. Below is a concise summary of Redwood’s proposed positions and the rationale, plus the specific draft language we suggest for the MSA and Order Form.

Summary (short):
- Output ownership: Redwood will accept language that the Customer retains ownership of Outputs generated from Customer Data. Redwood requests a limited exception for Outputs that are based solely on Redwood-provided IP (e.g., system prompts or pre-provisioned templates).
- Training/feedback: Redwood will not use Customer Data to train or fine-tune models unless Customer provides an explicit opt-in. Redwood requests a limited, narrowly-scoped feedback license to use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for quality improvements and to debug service issues. This license expressly excludes PII/PHI and any Customer Confidential Information.
- Implementation: We will add an opt-out checkbox in the Order Form for training; if Customer selects "No Training," we will exclude their data from any improvement pipelines and document the isolation controls. There may be a small commercial uplift to cover operational segregation costs; Aditya and I will include suggested pricing options.

Proposed contract snippets (MSA):
- "Customer Outputs": "Customer retains all right, title and interest in and to Outputs generated by the Services from Customer Data, subject to Redwood’s ownership of its pre-existing models and system-provided content. Outputs do not include Redwood Confidential Information or any derivative model parameters."

- "Feedback and Improvements": "Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to use Feedback (as defined below) solely to operate, maintain and improve the Redwood service, provided that Feedback does not include Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, PII or PHI. 'Feedback' means aggregated, de-identified usage metrics and system performance data. Redwood shall not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune or re-train any model without the Customer's prior written consent (which may be provided via explicit opt-in in the Order Form)."

Order Form language (checkbox approach):
- "Training Opt-Out": "Customer may elect to opt-out of Redwood using Customer Data to train or improve models. If Customer elects to opt-out, Redwood will: (a) exclude Customer Data from model training pipelines; (b) provide written documentation of isolation controls upon request; and (c) may charge a mutually-agreed commercial uplift to cover segregation costs."

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether Meridian can accept the proposed Output definition and the Feedback license carveout.
2) If acceptable, Elena — we will return a redlined MSA and Order Form today (attached) with tracked changes and a one-page summary table of changes for your legal.
3) If Meridian requires additional carveouts (e.g., complete prohibition of any telemetry), let us know what you need and we’ll highlight the operational implications.

Attachments: Redwood_redline_Meridian_MSA_v3.docx, Redline_Summary_Table.xlsx

Happy to hop on a short call if that helps move to signature.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Associate General Counsel
Redwood Inference
